 Order
This matter is taken up through hybrid arrangement (virtual/physical) mode.

2. The petitioners by way of this writ petition invoke the extra ordinary writ jurisdiction of this Court with following relief:
"II. issue writ in the nature of certiorari and quash the Notice No. Dated 14.11.2022 (ANNEXURE-14) and 02.03.2023 (ANNEXURE-17) both issued by the Collector,
Jajpur in acquiring the Stithiban Land of the Petitioners appertaining to Khata No.
34, Plot No. 476, Kissam- Gharabari, Area- Ac. 0.113 dec. and Plot No. 477, Kissam- Jalasaya, Area- Ac. 0.027 dec. of Mouza- Unit No. 7, Sitaleswar, P.S.- Jajpur (No.
210), Tahsil/Dist- Jajpur, Odisha and the order dated 11.05.2023 passed in Misc.
Case No. 61 of 2023 (ANNEXURE-18) and consequential Notice dated 20.07.2023 (ANNEXURE-19) as illegal, arbitrary and passed without following due process of law as prescribed under The Orissa Municipal Act, 1950 and the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013".
3.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Mr. S.S.Mohanty, learned counsel for the petitioners while reiterating the facts and highlighting the provision of Section 20 of // 2 // the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (in short, "RFCTLR &R") submits that the opposite parties have not prepared any plan and thereby, the propose acquisition of private land of the petitioners in clear violation of guidelines by way of notification dated 14.11.2022 is unjust,
arbitrary and illegal and therefore, the notice under Annexures-14, 17 and 19 as well as the order passed under Annexure-18 cannot sustain.

sentences.text:
After having considered the rival submission and upon perusal of record, it appears that the petitioners had raised objection to the acquisition of land for want of compliance of Section 20 of RFCTLR & R and the Collector, Jajpur in disposing the same in his order under Annexure-18 has observed the followings:-
"xxx It is pertinent to mention here that after according due approval of the scheme and plan of Govt. in the relevant Department the above notification and declaration have been issued xxx".
It is, therefore, clear that the objection of the petitioners on the above score is not acceptable.

5. Besides, perusal of the averments taken in the writ petition, reveals that the petitioners accept or consent for the part acquisition of land to the extent of 7ft. and it appears from the order of the Collector that acquisition of excess land i.e. more than the requirement of the road project stands as the need for drainage as well as widening of the road to avoid accident and traffic jam as the junction will have major footfall of the patients and students in the Hospital.
6.

In view of the aforesaid backdrop and situation, especially when the acquisition of land is found to be in the public interest for // 3 // construction of the road, the claim of the petitioners merits no consideration.
7. Accordingly, the writ petition is dismissed.
(D. Dash) Judge (G. Satapathy) Judge Kishore/Subhasmita Signed by: KISHORE KUMAR SAHOO
